raw_response:
I have farmed 30 years, and on 4.1 mu I do not like taking big risks. I start from what usually works here, then I adjust a little for water, price, and labor. Since I have well irrigation, I will not keep fertilizer too low, because if I save a little on fertilizer and lose yield, that loss is bigger than the fertilizer money. With my size, every bag matters, so I will split the land instead of betting everything on one crop. I will keep a little more land in stevia because the cropping system is already set that way, but I will still keep some cotton. For cotton, I will use improved seed, plough once, put most phosphorus and part of nitrogen and potassium as base fertilizer, then topdress in stages after squaring and at early flowering. Cotton here cannot be short of potash if I want bolls to hold well. For stevia, I will use improved seedlings, make the land fine with rotary tillage, use enough base manure or compound fertilizer if I have it, then add nitrogen in 2 times after establishment and after the first strong growth. Stevia needs steady water, so I will irrigate more often than cotton but not flood it. For pests, I will not wait too long. On a small field I can watch it closely, and once I see aphids, bollworm, mite, or leaf problems getting up, I will spray in time instead of letting it spread.
